Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the call this morning — helpful overview from your side. We want to make sure we pick the right deployment mode for our initial rollout and get a ballpark on cost. A couple of notes from our end:

- Primary use case: customer support summarization + routing, ~3M monthly incoming messages, average request size ~750 tokens.
- Latency SLO: <300ms 95th for short responses (50-150 tokens), some longer summaries okay at 500-800ms.
- Data requirements: logs stored for 30 days; PII redaction required; must be SOC2 compliant.
- Preference: if costs make sense, we'd prefer Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput, but we need to understand tradeoffs vs Hosted API and Private VPC.

Attached is a short requirements doc (acme_requirements.pdf). Can you send a post-call recap with next steps and a rough cost model (hosted per-token vs dedicated reserved commit)? Also cc procurement contact Liam (cc'd).

Emma — thanks for the clear notes and the requirements doc. Recap + next steps below:

Recap:
- Use case: CS summarization + routing; ~3M requests/mo, 750 tokens avg.
- SLO: 95th <300ms for short responses; sensitive data handling + SOC2 required.
- Preference: leaning toward Dedicated, but want cost comparison.

Quick guidance on deployment modes:
- Hosted API: fastest to get started, pay-as-you-go per-token. Good if you want to avoid commit but unit cost is higher and there can be noisy-neighbor variance.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU capacity (monthly/annual commits). Lower per-token cost at scale and predictable latency. Better for steady high throughput like your 3M/mo.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): for strict data residency or air-gapped setups. Higher setup/ops and usually reserved contract.

Requested next steps:
1) I’ll loop in Marissa (SE) to run a quick cost model — she’ll propose a 1/3/12-month commit comparison (hosted per-token, monthly reserved, annual reserved) and include expected latency profiles.
2) Please confirm retention + encryption/KMS needs (from your requirements doc I noted 30-day logs + PII redaction). Any additional compliance evidence needed beyond SOC2?
3) If Dedicated looks right, we’ll introduce Neha (sales lead) to scope contract/commits and timelines.

Tentative timeline: Marissa will send a cost model by tomorrow EOD PDT. From there we can schedule a short follow-up to review numbers and procurement asks.

Thanks again — looping in Marissa and Neha.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Account Executive

Hi Emma / Aditya — attaching an initial cost model (redwood_cost_model.xlsx) and a short summary below. This is an estimate based on the numbers you shared (3M requests/mo, ~750 tokens/request).

Attachment: redwood_cost_model.xlsx (spreadsheet stub — request rows: traffic, token assumptions, reserved capacity sizing, monthly and annual commit pricing, TCO)

Summary of estimates (ballpark):
- Hosted API (pay-as-you-go per-token):~ $0.0009 per token effective at current model mix => ~ $2,025,000 / month (high-level; includes generation + embedding usage).
- Dedicated Monthly Reserved (1x A100 equivalent pool sized for 3M requests): equivalent unit economics reduce to ~ $900,000 / month. Pricing assumes moderate batching and prefix caching.
- Dedicated Annual Commit (12-month): further discounted to ~ $650,000 / month effective.
- Private/VPC: add one-time onboarding (~$75k) + higher base reserved pricing; recommended only if you need isolated control plane or on-prem constraints.

Notes & assumptions:
- We assumed average output tokens per request 750; if your summaries are shorter (300-400 tokens) costs drop proportionally.
- Batching and KV caching can significantly reduce tokens served if many requests share prefixes (we can run a quick sample eval).
- Dedicated pricing above includes minimum SLA and reserved GPU capacity; exact instance sizing depends on concurrency and latency SLOs.

Recommended next steps:
1) If you'd like, we can run a short sample (1 week) against a production-ish prompt set to estimate effective token usage and caching benefits.
2) Confirm whether 30-day retention + SOC2 + KMS are sufficient. If you need PCI/PHI-level controls or private hosting, we’ll provide a Private deployment quote.
3) Aditya/Neha will coordinate procurement and contract terms once you pick a preferred deployment mode.

Let me know if you want a quick call to walk through the spreadsheet today.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer
